All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2002) * Fourth-team ''Parade'' All-American (2001) }} '''Rashad Dion McCants''' (born September 25, 1984) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who has played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) as well as overseas. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]], winning a [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball champions|national championship]] in his junior season. Currently, he is part of the cast for [[Gilbert Arenas]]' podcast titled "The Arena" alongside [[Lexie Brown]], [[Brandon Jennings]], [[Kenyon Martin]], and [[Nick Young]].{{cite web|title=The Arena|url=https://www.youtube.com/@TheArena0}} ==High school career== McCants began his high school career at [[Clyde A. Erwin High School]]{{cite web | last = Goodman | first = Jeff | title = Basketball Recruiting Buzz | publisher = ESPN | url = https://a.espncdn.com/highschool/a/000201bballbuzz.html | access-date = March 30, 2022}} in [[Asheville, North Carolina]], and finished at [[New Hampton School]] in [[New Hampton, New Hampshire|New Hampton]], [[New Hampshire]]. He led New Hampton to the 2002 New England Prep School Class A championship and was named [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] of the title game. McCants played alongside future college teammate [[Wes Miller]] during his senior season.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} McCants was an honor roll student at New Hampton.[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/rashad_mccants/bio.html NBA.com : Rashad McCants Bio Page] He also won the New Hampshire Player of the Year Award in 2001 and 2002. And, as a senior, he was also named to the Parade All-American and [[McDonald's All-American Team]]s. He played in the McDonald's All-American Game with future Tar Heel teammates [[Raymond Felton]] and [[Sean May]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} {{College athlete recruit start|year=2002}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Rashad McCants | position = SG, SF | hometown = [[Asheville, North Carolina|Asheville, NC]] | highschool = [[New Hampton School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 200 | 40 = | commitdate = | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 4 }} {{College athlete recruit end | year = 2002 | rivals ref title = 2002 North Carolina Basketball Commitment List | scout ref title = 2002 North Carolina College Basketball Recruiting Commits | rivals school = northcarolina | scout s = 78 | scout overall = 1 (SG) | rivals overall = 4 (SF) | accessdate = August 10, 2014 | archivedate = | rivals archiveurl= | scout archiveurl = | 247 archiveurl = | espn archiveurl = | bball = yes }} ==College career== Alongside [[Sean May]], [[Raymond Felton]], and [[David Noel]], McCants joined a stellar recruiting class at UNC for the 2002–2003 season, coached by [[Matt Doherty (basketball)|Matt Doherty]]. In his freshman year, McCants led the Tar Heels in scoring with 17.5 points per game, and led them to a third round loss to [[Georgetown Hoyas|Georgetown]] in the [[National Invitational Tournament]]. He was voted to the All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) rookie team.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} In the 2003–2004 season, McCants led the ACC in scoring with 20 points per game. With that effort, McCants helped lead UNC back into the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] with a sixth seed, where they lost in the second round to number three seeded Texas. He was the leading vote-getter on the All-ACC First Team as a sophomore, and was named a third-team [[All-American]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}} With freshman [[Marvin Williams]] joining the squad for the 2004–2005 season, the junior class led by preseason [[Wooden Award]] candidates in McCants, May, and Felton gave UNC a high ranking in all preseason polls and the team was seen as one of the favorites to win the NCAA Tournament. After going 33–4 and winning the ACC regular season, McCants' 16.4 points per game helped secure UNC one of the four number one seeds in the NCAA Tournament. UNC cruised to the championship game, where McCants helped the Tar Heels defeat the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|Illinois]] Fighting Illini, 75–70.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/article/unc-rashad-mccants-on-the-2005-national-titleteam-148314150/|title=Rashad McCants on UNC's Magical 2005 National Title Team|last=Martin|first=Ross|date=June 19, 2020|website=Inside Carolina|access-date=January 9, 2024}} McCants' three years at [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|Chapel Hill]] were not without controversy. In an interview with local television station [[WRAL-TV|WRAL]], McCants compared UNC to a prison, stating, "You're not allowed to say certain things, but once you get out of jail, you're free. (I'm) in my sentence, and I'm doing my time."{{cite web|url=https://www.wralsportsfan.com/rs/story/1090689/|title=McCants Compares UNC Basketball To Job, Prison|publisher=WRAL-TV|date=October 19, 2004|access-date=July 30, 2014}}{{cite web|last1=Parsons|first1=Keith|title=McCants: 'I love North Carolina'|url=http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/101904abb.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808044809/http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/101904abb.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 8, 2014 |publisher=Associated Press|access-date=July 30, 2014|date=October 19, 2004}} Original AP wire title: "McCants Says He Likes Being at Carolina" McCants scored 1,721 points and made 221 [[three-point field goal|three-pointers]] during his career at North Carolina.{{cite web|url=https://goheels.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/rashad-mccants/10782|title=Rashad McCants Bio – 2004-05 Men's Basketball Roster|publisher=[[North Carolina Tar Heels]]|access-date=January 9, 2024}} ==Professional career== After winning the championship, McCants declared his eligibility for the [[2005 NBA draft]], and was selected 14th overall by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. His college teammates, [[Marvin Williams]], [[Raymond Felton]], and [[Sean May]] were also selected in the draft. During his first two years as a pro, McCants was bothered by injuries and did not play up to the expectations of fans. He had a lot of expectations going into the 2007–08 season, and on a young Timberwolves squad, he started the season as a rotation regular, and broke into the starting lineup halfway through the season. As of January 2008, Rashad had posted career-highs through his third season, with 34 points against the [[Denver Nuggets]] on January 4, 2008,[https://web.archive.org/web/20080108080909/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280104016 Iverson nets 33 as Nuggets cruise past Timberwolves] 8 rebounds against the [[Miami Heat]] on January 8,[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/rashad_mccants/career_stats.html NBA.com : Rashad McCants Career Stats Page] 4 steals against the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] on December 29, 2007, and getting 6 assists five times. On December 26, 2008, he hit a career-high 7 three-pointers in a Wolves win over the [[New York Knicks]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20081230075210/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=281226018 Timberwolves end 13-game skid, hand McHale first win as coach] On February 19, 2009, McCants was sent to the [[Sacramento Kings]] along with [[Calvin Booth]] for [[Shelden Williams]] and [[Bobby Brown (basketball)|Bobby Brown]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/Press_Release_021909.html |title=KINGS ACQUIRE RASHAD McCANTS AND CALVIN BOOTH |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=2009-02-19 |accessdate=2009-02-19}} McCants then signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] in September 2009,[http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/6635141.html Rockets sign former Tar Heels star McCants]. Retrieved on September 24, 2009. but had his contract retracted on the second day of the training camp. The Rockets General Manager said McCants presented with an abdomen problem and would not be able to participate in the camp, though he also said he would still consider McCants down the track once healthy.{{Citation needed|date=February 2010}} In the summer of 2010, he was scheduled to join the Cleveland Cavaliers' [[NBA Summer League]] team. However, he did not report to the team for personal reasons.{{cite web|last=Windhorst|first=Brian|title=Another strong summer-league effort by J.J. Hickson keeps Cleveland Cavaliers coaches smiling|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2010/07/another_strong_summer-league_e.html|work=Cleveland.com|date=17 July 2010 |accessdate=19 July 2010}} In October 2010 the Dallas Mavericks signed McCants to their training camp roster. However, he was released only after a few days. He was then signed by the Mavericks' NBA Development League associate, the Texas Legends. In 2012, the [[Powerade Tigers]] of the Philippine Basketball Association acquired him as their import for the Governors Cup. However, despite playing his usual game, he was not able to help the Tigers win their first two games and was released afterwards. On July 13, 2012, McCants signed with the French club [[Strasbourg IG]].{{cite web|last=|first=|title=SIG Strasbourg officially signs Rashad McCants ==BIG3== On April 30, 2017, McCants was selected as the No. 1 overall pick in the 2017 [[BIG3]] Draft by [[Trilogy (basketball)|Trilogy]].{{cite news|title=2017 BIG3 draft results|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2017/4/30/15494430/big3-draft-results-2017-rashad-mccants-steve-francis|access-date=July 15, 2017|work=sbnation.com|date=April 30, 2017}} On August 26, 2017, Trilogy won the first-ever Big3 League Championship. McCants scored 22 points on 55% shooting and was named Championship MVP.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/big3-championship-former-nba-players-harrington-martin-win-inaugural-title/|title=BIG3 Championship: Former NBA players Harrington, Martin win inaugural title|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-08-27|language=en}} ==Personal life== McCants' sister, [[Rashanda McCants]], also played for [[North Carolina Tar Heels women's basketball|North Carolina]] and in the [[WNBA]].{{cite news|last1=McCann|first1=Michael|last2=Wertheim|first2=Jon|title=Rashanda McCants, Devon Ramsay file suit against UNC, NCAA|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/01/06/rashanda-mccants-unc-paper-classes-lawsuit|access-date=5 April 2016|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=January 22, 2015}} Rashad is the cousin of [[Major League Baseball]] player [[Cameron Maybin]] and third cousin of former [[Canadian Football League]] player [[John Avery (gridiron football)|John Avery]].[http://www.ahsweb1973.com/Ahsweb/Special.aspx The Asheville High, Class of 73, Current Photos] In June 2008, McCants began dating reality television star [[Khloe Kardashian]]. The two were introduced by the [[National Football League]] player [[Reggie Bush]] who had been dating her sister [[Kim Kardashian|Kim]] at the time.{{cite news|last=Gartland|first=Dan|title=Rashad McCants: I wouldn't have washed out of the NBA if I didn't date Khloe Kardashian|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/05/25/rashad-mccants-khloe-kardashian-nba-career-bust|access-date=30 May 2020|agency=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=25 May 2017}} The relationship ended after seven months, in late January 2009, reportedly due to McCants's [[infidelity]].{{cite news|last=Lane|first=Laura|title=Khloe Kardashian Calls Ex a "Loser"|url=https://okmagazine.com/news/khloe-kardashian-calls-ex-loser/|access-date=30 May 2020|agency=[[OK!]]|date=5 February 2009}} He also made a brief guest appearance on her reality show, ''[[Keeping Up with the Kardashians]]'', during [[List of Keeping Up with the Kardashians episodes#Season 3 (2009)|season 3 (episode 7)]]. Eight years later, speaking with a ''[[The Charlotte Observer|Charlotte Observer]]'' reporter while looking back on his career in the NBA, McCants stated that the highly publicized relationship with Khloe Kardashian was the "biggest regret" because it "gave people an opportunity to doubt his commitment to the NBA", adding: "Without that situation in play, I’m a $60-70 million player. Easily."{{cite news|last=Cowart|first=C Jackson|title=Ex-UNC star Rashad McCants says relationship with school, coach Roy Williams no longer exists|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nba/article152450349.html|access-date=30 May 2020|agency=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=24 May 2017}} McCants was one of the victims of Williams]], [[Travis Best]], [[Dennis Rodman]], [[Lex Hilliard]] and others.{{Cite magazine |title=The Peggy Show: Every athlete's worst nightmare |last=Prewitt |first=Alex |date=2019-09-19
